title: Machine-learning screening identified three compounds with measured ULK1 inhibition
summary: A Gaussian naive-Bayes classifier using ECFP6 fingerprints ranked commercial compounds from a 13-million-compound library, followed by docking, property filtering and manual selection. Researchers purchased and assayed 25 candidates; three showed micromolar ULK1 inhibition, with reported IC50 values of 37.11 ± 4.41, 7.67 ± 2.82 and 3.15 ± 0.77 μM. The molecules were purchased rather than newly synthesized, and this entry does not claim absolute chemical novelty. The study’s comparator MRT68921 was more potent; the results do not establish cellular activity or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Gaussian naive-Bayes classifier on ECFP6 molecular fingerprints (NB-ECFP6)
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University; Oujiang Laboratory; Wenzhou Medical University; Macao Polytechnic University

evidence.tested: The paper reports 25 purchased candidates tested in a biochemical ULK1 kinase assay; three had measured micromolar inhibition with IC50 values 37.11 ± 4.41, 7.67 ± 2.82 and 3.15 ± 0.77 μM.
evidence.unknown: The candidates were purchased, not synthesized. The reported assays do not establish cell activity or clinical effect; the reference MRT68921 was more potent in the paper’s comparison. Absolute structure novelty is not claimed here.
evidence.ai_role: The NB-ECFP6 model screened a large commercial compound set and prioritized candidates for downstream docking and biochemical testing.
